Whether the national security ministry publicly backs, contradicts or slow-walks the police investigation.
decode.easy: Israel's prime minister called the settler attacks on two Palestinian villages criminal, which he rarely does. But so far the army has only impounded some cars and nobody has been arrested — and over twenty years, 94 out of every 100 of these police files have closed with no charges at all.

decode.claim: The prompt reaction of Niger's defence and security forces contained the mutiny and gradually regained control of the sites attacked in Niamey.
decode.source: Niger junta statement read on state television
decode.verdictNote: Partly true — and the tell is inside the wording. A government that held its capital does not need to announce that it “gradually regained control” of sensitive sites; the sentence concedes the sites were lost before it claims they were recovered. Containment itself looks real — the state broadcaster came back on air, and the presidential guard repelled an attempt on the palace — but a diplomatic source told AFP the guard retook the air base “with the help of the Russians,” which, if confirmed, means the regime's own forces were not sufficient. That is the part of the day that has consequences, and it is not in the statement.
decode.reality: Sustained gunfire and explosions were reported on Aug 29 around Base 101, the presidential palace and the state broadcaster in Niamey. Soldiers from the Base 101 barracks opened fire on several sensitive sites after attempting to detain fellow soldiers. Télé Sahel went off air for about an hour before being restored around 10:00. Security sources confirmed an attempted breach of the presidential palace was pushed back by the presidential guard. This is the latest challenge to Abdourahamane Tiani, who took power in the 2023 coup.
decode.aspiration: Almost every operational detail. No casualty figures, no confirmed arrests, no confirmation of airport status, no named plotters, and — the absence that matters most — no dated public appearance by Tiani himself. The Russian assistance rests on a single anonymous diplomatic source and has not been confirmed or denied by Niamey or Moscow. “Contained” is a claim about a moving situation made by the party with the strongest interest in it being over.

angles.effect: Survive the day and acquire a licence for a purge of the officer corps — the standard post-mutiny move, and the one that tells you how frightened they actually were. Watch the arrest list, not the statement.

angles.party: The mutineers, reported as junior officers
angles.effect: If they are named and tried publicly, the regime is confident. If the files stay sealed and the men disappear into detention, it is not — secrecy after a failed coup usually indicates the plot reached higher than the government wants known.

angles.party: Russia and its Africa Corps presence
angles.effect: If the air base really was retaken with Russian help, Moscow converts a security service into standing political leverage over Niamey — over uranium contracts, over basing, over what Niger can refuse later. Protection is the most expensive thing a weak government can accept, and France and the US, already expelled from their Niger bases, have no instrument left to compete for it.

angles.party: The Sahel alliance partners, Mali and Burkina Faso
angles.effect: A wobble in Niamey wobbles all three. Their juntas rest on the same arithmetic of junior officers with weapons and grievances, and each attempt raises the perceived odds for the next — as it does for the uranium buyers repricing supply risk who were consulted by nobody.

Pay in curfews, communications cuts and a security establishment that now has to watch itself as well as the jihadist insurgency in Tillabéri — attention diverted from the threat that actually kills them.

clock.d90: Arrests, a military tribunal, and a reshuffle of the general staff or the presidential guard command. Also whether Tiani appears in person, on a dated broadcast — the cheapest proof of control there is.
clock.m18: Whether the purge stabilises the army or seeds the next attempt, and whether any Russian role formalises into a written basing or training agreement.
clock.y7: The base rate governs. Niger has now seen repeated coups and attempts; a regime that survives by purging its officer corps tends to meet the same event again, and each round narrows the pool of officers it can trust.

watch: A published list of arrested officers and the convening of a military tribunal — names and ranks, not a numbered total.
Tiani appearing in person on state television, with a verifiable date.
An official Nigerien or Russian statement confirming or denying Russian participation at Base 101 — the single missing document that would change the read of the whole day.
Reopening of Diori Hamani international airport and a return to published flight schedules.
Changes to the command of the presidential guard or the army general staff in the next gazette.
decode.easy: Soldiers attacked the presidential palace and an air base in Niger's capital, and the government says it contained the mutiny and took the sites back. Saying you “gradually regained control” admits you lost them first — and a diplomatic source says Russian forces helped, which would mean the government now owes Moscow for its own survival.

easy.bottomLine: The most important thing today is that Iran fired missiles and drones at American air bases in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates. Kuwait's own army said it was shooting them down. Nobody American has been killed so far, but that is mostly because the air defences keep working - not because anyone has decided to stop. At the same time the price of oil jumped for the fourth day in a row and almost touched $100, and the number of ships getting through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to about six in a day, when a normal day is around eighty-five.
easy.risk: Still HIGH, now for a seventh day. The rule we wrote down before any of this started is that it only goes to the very top when an American is killed or an American ship is hit, and that still has not happened. What changed today is the map. Iran is now hitting bases in six different countries that host American forces, and the United Arab Emirates is the newest one. Careful readers should notice one thing: Iran says it destroyed hangars and warehouses, but no host country has confirmed any damage. We know the missiles were fired, because Kuwait said so. We do not know what they hit.
easy.markets: Oil is the story. Brent went for a fourth straight day of gains and traded near $97, with reports of it nearly touching $99 during the day - the highest since July. Diesel is worse than crude, and diesel is what moves lorries, tractors and delivery vans, so it ends up in the price of food. American petrol now averages $4.12 a gallon, about a dollar more than a year ago. Something else moved that most people will not have noticed: the Japanese yen jumped, because Japan looks likely to raise interest rates on 18 September. For thirty years investors have borrowed cheap Japanese money to buy things everywhere else, and when the yen goes up they have to sell those things to pay the loan back. That is how a decision in Tokyo can shake markets in New York.
brief: Iran fired missiles and drones at American air bases in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates overnight, and Kuwait's army said it was shooting them down. It is the sixth country hosting American troops to be hit in this war, and the American president said his forces are ready to attack Iran again any time they want.

Oil rose for a fourth day and came close to $100 a barrel, while only about six ships got through the Strait of Hormuz in a day instead of the usual eighty-five. Diesel is rising even faster than crude oil, and because diesel powers lorries and tractors, that shows up later in the price of food and almost everything else.

The Japanese yen jumped to a one-month high because Japan is expected to raise interest rates on 18 September. That sounds like a local story but it is not: for years people have borrowed cheap Japanese money to buy shares and bonds around the world, and when the yen rises they have to sell those to pay it back.

President Putin said a deal to end the war in Ukraine is possible and admitted that Russia and Ukraine are still talking - through their spy agencies rather than their diplomats. That matters more than the friendly words, because it is usually how wars actually get stopped. On the same day, Britain called in Russia's top diplomat over a drone attack on a German airport.

Spain's prime minister told parliament that nobody warned him before seventy thousand people crossed into the Spanish city of Ceuta in July, and that there is no proof Morocco planned it. But a police report given to a judge says Moroccan officers helped direct the crossing, and police are said to have sent two written warnings beforehand.

risk.line: Held at HIGH for a seventh day, and the published rule is the reason it does not move to the top: that step requires a confirmed American death or a struck US-flagged hull, and neither happened. What changed overnight is the map of who is absorbing the fire. Iran's army says it put missiles and suicide drones into Ahmed al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait - naming satellite communications, equipment warehouses and fighter hangars - and into US positions and radars at Al Minhad in the United Arab Emirates. Kuwait's army confirmed publicly that it was engaging missiles and drones launched from Iran. Read the confirmation carefully, because it is the honest limit of what we know: the LAUNCH is confirmed by a host government, the DAMAGE is claimed only by the party that fired. The UAE is the sixth host state to take fire in this campaign, and the interception rate is doing the work that a decision would normally do. Alongside it the President described a very heavy attack and said American forces are prepared to do another one any time we want, which is the diplomatic track being closed verbally rather than by any event. The market read the same page: Brent touched $99.38 intraday, a fourth straight up day, diesel futures went to a five-month high on top of a record crack spread, and transits through the strait fell to as few as six ships in a day against a normal count near eighty-five.

forecasts.q: Brent stays inside the $80-100 band
forecasts.note: CUT 19, by far the largest move this book has made, and a deliberate exception to its own small-moves rule. The reason is that this is a BARRIER question, and barrier probability is nonlinear in distance: Brent printed $99.38 intraday, up about $3.27 in a fourth consecutive up-session, settling roughly $95 to $97. The upper $100 barrier is now about 3.5 percent away against roughly 17 percent to the lower, so the question has become effectively one-sided. With about 21 calendar days and 14 trading sessions left and realized daily moves of 2 to 3 percent, remaining-window sigma is around 9 to 10 percent, which puts the near barrier only about a third of a standard deviation out; the reflection principle then gives a touch probability near 70 percent, and survival near 30, before any adjustment for upward drift. The distance to the barrier more than halved in one session, so one large re-mark is the correct response and a sequence of small cuts would only have been a slower way of being wrong. Two disciplines kept: this is NOT a directional oil call - it would have moved identically on a newsless three-dollar rally, which is why it is not counted in today's escalation cluster - and the wording still governs, since $99.38 was an INTRADAY print while the question resolves on daily closes. Nothing has breached

forecasts.q: Major US/Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes

Second, the diplomatic track was closed verbally from the top - a very heavy attack, prepared to do another one anytime we want, with wire coverage framing the President as dismissing diplomacy, while Iran's First Vice President promised asymmetric and multilayered tactics. FLAGGED AGAINST OURSELVES: at four consecutive nights against state air-defence, radar and communications targets, a reasonable adjudicator could already call this YES. We have been reading nightly barrages as an ongoing exchange rather than a resumed campaign, which is defensible but is an unstated wording choice doing real work, and it goes to the weekly audit rather than being absorbed by the number

Base rate first: moves of 8 percent or more in the yen inside thirty days are rare but recurrent - August 2024, when the unwind took the Nikkei down 12.4 percent in a session, the late-2022 intervention run, 2016, 2008 - roughly five episodes in twenty years, which over a seven-month window prices near 15. Written on the TRANSMISSION rather than on the BoJ decision, because the decision is a Japanese event and the transmission is the global one

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire holds 30+ days
forecasts.note: RAISED 2 on the first genuinely two-sided day in a week. Putin, at the Eastern Economic Forum, said there is a chance of an agreement and that a number of countries including the US and China are ready to support a settlement - and, the load-bearing detail, confirmed that contacts with Kyiv are continuing on an ongoing basis, primarily through intelligence channels. That is the Ratcliffe channel surviving the Kremlin's own deep pause statement of Aug 28, which is a fact about machinery rather than about mood. Ukraine's foreign minister said he expects a new dynamic; India's Jaishankar offered help after Modi pressed Putin on Monday. Framework is Reiter's expectation-convergence - belligerents settle when their estimates of the future converge, and a surviving back-channel is the standard precursor to formal talks. Capped at 2 by three offsets kept in front: Putin's very next sentence returned the problem to the two belligerents, which is an explicit refusal of a third-party mechanism; London summoned Russia's charge d'affaires over the Leipzig airport attack the same day, so the coalition-punishment track is still widening; and Ukraine at four and a half years is deep in the right tail of the distribution where about 79 percent of interstate wars have already ended

NAMED COUNTER, kept in view: Fed officials are now openly weighing a rate RISE while Waller leans to hold, and a hawkish turn is a live argument for sunsetting the program to buy inflation credibility

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Iran hits US bases in Kuwait and UAE as Trump waves off diplomacy
brief.h: Iran's army said it fired missiles and suicide drones early on 3 September at Ahmed al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait - naming satellite communications systems, equipment warehouses and fighter-jet hangars - and at US positions and radar systems at Al Minhad Air Base in the United Arab Emirates, which becomes the sixth host state to take fire in this war; Kuwait's army confirmed publicly that it was confronting hostile missile and drone attacks launched from Iran and its foreign ministry condemned a violation of sovereignty, Bahrain also reported interceptions, and Saudi Arabia called for de-escalation and a return to negotiations, while President Trump described a very heavy attack on Iranian targets and said American forces are prepared to do another one any time we want, and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref promised asymmetric and multilayered tactics ahead.
brief.t: The important thing here is not that Iran fired again - it is where the fire is landing, and what is actually holding this war below the line. Nothing anyone decided is keeping Americans alive tonight; an interception rate is. Iran fires target-matched volleys at hardened bases, air defences catch most of them, and both governments get to claim a result - Tehran shows retaliation to its own public, Washington shows no casualties to its own. That is an equilibrium made of arithmetic, and arithmetic degrades: every new launch site and every new host country adds another draw from the same probability distribution, and equilibria fail at their widest edge rather than their centre. The bargain underneath is the one nobody in the Gulf voted on. Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and the Emirates sold basing rights for security guarantees after 1991, and this week they are discovering the price is denominated in their own sovereignty - their air defences, their airspace, their citizens under the intercept. Our number for a resumed multi-day campaign against Iranian state targets goes to 43 percent, and the flag we are putting on ourselves is that at four consecutive nights of strikes on radars, air defences and now communications towers, a fair adjudicator might already call that question closed.
brief.context: The rail is older than the crisis and explains why Iran can reach Kuwait and Dubai at all: the Gulf basing architecture was built after 1991, when Desert Storm converted temporary access into permanent infrastructure, and every one of those bases sits inside Iranian short-range fires by geography rather than by choice. The permit is newer - once a war aim is publicly stated as removing a government, strikes on state targets stop needing a discrete casus belli and become maintenance. The desk that decides is not the podium: it is the delegated strike-approval level inside CENTCOM, because a target cleared by a two-star on a fifteen-minute clock is a different object from one cleared in Washington over three days, and it is each ruling family's own political calculus about how much visible cost hosting is worth. Base rate, stated honestly against our own position: militarized disputes escalate to full war in low single-digit percentages and no dispute initiated since 2001 has done so - but a chokepoint toll regime enforced under fire is close to unprecedented, so the reference class is thin and the model uncertainty is real. The influence map runs: Tehran's Guard as principal, the army as the signing agent, state television as narrator, the air-defence crews of six host states as the operators who decide the outcome, the Brent futures curve as the market that prices it, and Gulf civilians as the target who never had a seat. What would change the read is a single observable - a host state publicly restricting American offensive use of its soil, which converts venues into parties.

angles.effect: Gains a demonstration it can sell at home for the cost of munitions it was going to lose anyway. Note what it does NOT gain: no host government has confirmed damage, so the claim about hangars and warehouses is worth exactly what an unverified communique is worth.

Gains the strongest argument it has - a clean interception record - and pays in commitment. Every night the equilibrium holds is another night the deployment order has to be extended, and it now runs into 2027 over three combatant commanders' formal objections.

Pay the bill nobody priced when the bases were built. They must condemn Iran to protect sovereignty and simultaneously avoid becoming co-belligerents, which is why the language is violation of sovereignty rather than act of war - a deliberate, load-bearing choice of words.

Gains from staying out loud and staying out. Calling for de-escalation while others take the fire is the cheapest possible position and confirms that Riyadh reads this as a war it can outlast rather than one it must join.
Pay in freight and insurance without any voice in it - India, China, Japan and Korea take most of the barrels that cross this strait and none of them is in the room where the escalation is decided.

dec.kill: A host government - not Iran - confirming physical damage at Ahmed al-Jaber or Al Minhad, or CENTCOM releasing a battle-damage assessment. That would convert Iran's claim from a communique into a fact. Conversely, a fortnight of quiet with Muscat publishing corridor coordinates or a minesweeping calendar kills our recurrence read outright, and we have dated that falsifier to 22 September so it can be scored against us.

consp.claim: That both of America's live wars were sold as short operations and are being fought as multi-year campaigns, and that the fraud is in the framing rather than in any single battlefield claim - the boards keep the tally in the thread header itself, currently Day 188 of what they call the four-day operation to change the government of Iran.
consp.spread: The long-running Persia Israel General on 4chan's /pol/ has carried that header for months at 250-plus replies a thread, and the same construction now circulates on X across both the anti-interventionist right and the anti-war left.
consp.read: The duration-fraud frame, and it is the most durable narrative on the board because it needs no evidence beyond a calendar. The checkable kernel is entirely true: the campaign was publicly sold as short, it is in its 188th day, and the Pentagon's deployment order now reaches into 2027 over formal objections from three combatant commanders. What the frame adds on top is intent - that the short framing was deliberate deception rather than genuine misjudgement - and that part is unfalsifiable, because planning failure and calculated understatement produce identical calendars. The useful discipline is to keep the checkable half and discard the mind-reading.

brief.head: Brent nears $99 as Hormuz traffic falls to six ships a day
brief.h: Crude rose for a fourth consecutive session on the fourth night of strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent trading near $97 - its highest since 23 July - and market-data commentary reporting an intraday print close to $99.38 before settlement fell back into the $95 to $97 range, while US crude held above $92; the sharper move was in products, where ICE gasoil, the global diesel benchmark, rose as much as 4.2 per cent to its highest since 9 April on top of a crack spread that set a record last month, and transits through the strait fell to as few as six vessels in a day against a ten-day rolling average near thirteen and a pre-war norm around eighty-five; the US retail petrol average stands at $4.12 a gallon, up close to a dollar year on year, with diesel near $6.
brief.t: Watch the product, not the crude - that is where this story actually lives. Anyone can buy a barrel; almost nobody can turn one into diesel on short notice, because refineries are configured for particular grades and take years and billions to reconfigure. So when the diesel crack spread - the margin between a barrel of crude and the diesel refined out of it - prints a record while crude itself is only at a six-week high, the market is telling you the shortage is in refining and shipping capacity, not in oil in the ground. That matters because diesel is not a consumer product, it is an input: it prices freight, farming, construction and the delivery of everything else, which is how a chokepoint eleven thousand kilometres away arrives in a supermarket. And note the configuration underneath, which is the tell this desk watches for: oil is rising while the broad dollar sits at 118.75, near its highs. Oil and the dollar going up together is not the normal risk-on pattern - it is the squeeze pattern, in which every importer pays twice, once in the barrel and once in the currency it must buy the barrel with. Our band forecast on Brent staying inside $80 to $100 through 24 September fell today from 51 to 32 percent, and it fell on geometry rather than on opinion: the upper barrier is now about three and a half percent away.
brief.context: Date the rail before reading the headline. This is a late chapter of the 1973-79 epoch, when oil was yoked to the dollar and the settlement of energy became a political object - and its specific modern feature is that a chokepoint now generates a toll rather than an embargo. The physical board: roughly a fifth of the world's LNG and a large share of its crude crosses this strait, Russian refining fell to about 3.6m barrels a day in July on Ukrainian strikes - a 24-year low - with a product export ban running past 1 September, and European gas sits near a three-year high with storage about seventeen points below the seasonal norm. Those three facts are one fact: the product layer is the binding constraint everywhere at once. Forecast in stages, with falsifiers attached, because most energy shocks fizzle at the first one. Stage A, live now: prices grind higher on transit counts and product spreads - falsified by transits recovering above forty a day, which would take crude back toward the middle of the band. Stage B, within about sixty days: a policy palliative rather than a supply answer - a fuel-tax suspension, an SPR release, or a Gulf producer lifting quota - falsified if none appears by mid-November with petrol still above $4. Stage C, the one people reach for too fast: a genuine physical shortfall in diesel that shows up as rationing or industrial curtailment rather than as price - falsified by inventories holding through the winter, and we will score its non-arrival against the model rather than deferring it. Most of these stories end at A or B; this desk's standing warning is against making the collapse ending the conclusion of every energy story.

angles.effect: Gains from the cleared-lanes framing while paying for it at the pump. Having declared the corridor functioning on 28 August, every subsequent attack inside it is a claim the government has to keep re-purchasing rather than a new event it can point at.

Gain outright. A record diesel crack is a transfer from everyone who burns fuel to the small number of refineries able to run difficult crude, which is why the White House convened Valero, Marathon, PBF and Chevron rather than the drillers.

Gains revenue per barrel on the barrels it still moves, and gains coercive leverage priced daily in a public market. A blockade that raises the value of the cargo it cannot stop is a strange instrument, and that asymmetry is the whole file.
Pay hardest and are absent from every negotiation. Kenyan fuel prices are up about half; importing countries with no seat at any table carry the second-order incidence of a chokepoint war.
Pay on a lag through diesel rather than through petrol, which is the half of the inflation problem that does not appear on a roadside sign.

dec.kill: Transits recovering above forty vessels a day for two consecutive weeks, or a war-risk downgrade of the southern corridor by the Joint War Committee - either would show the cleared-lanes claim describing reality rather than aspiration. Conversely a strike on Kharg's loading terminals, as opposed to its military sites, would end the argument in the other direction and re-rate three of our forecasts at once.

consp.claim: That somebody with advance knowledge of American Iran policy has been trading oil futures ahead of announcements - the specific instances circulated are a bet of more than $500m on falling prices about fifteen minutes before the President posted a delay to strikes on 23 March, roughly $950m before the April ceasefire announcement, and $1.7bn of contracts changing hands about an hour before a report that sent crude tumbling on 6 May.
consp.spread: Very wide and mainstream-adjacent rather than fringe: it was reported by ABC News, NBC News and Forbes as a Justice Department and CFTC inquiry, and from there it became a fixed reference point on r/conspiracy, finance X and the /biz/ market threads, where it is cited whenever oil moves before news does.
consp.read: The insider-foreknowledge frame, and it is the rare one where the underlying artefact is a documented federal investigation rather than an inference. The checkable core is strong: the trades, the timestamps and the probe are all reported, and investigators are separately examining prediction-market activity on the same events, which is harder to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. The overreach is in what it is taken to prove - a probe is not a charge, no trader has been identified, and skilled opportunism by someone who simply reads the same signals faster produces the same tape. Our own tracked version of this hypothesis was CUT this week rather than raised, precisely because the most violently market-moving fortnight of the war produced no new episode; a theory that only ever explains the past is not doing work.

brief.head: Yen jumps to a one-month high as Tokyo readies a rate rise
brief.h: The yen strengthened more than one per cent against the dollar on 3 September to 156.15, a one-month high, after hawkish comments from Bank of Japan policymakers raised bets on a rate rise at the 18 September meeting and revived open talk of intervention; the ten-year Japanese government bond yield has reached about 3 per cent, its highest since 1996, with the five-year at a record 2.26 per cent and the policy rate already at 0.75 per cent, a thirty-year high, as import-driven inflation and wage growth push the central bank further from the era in which Japanese money was free.
brief.t: This looks like a domestic Japanese story and it is not - it is a story about where the world borrows. For most of thirty years Japan has been the planet's cheap funding leg: you borrow yen at almost nothing, sell them, and buy something that yields more - Mexican bonds, American tech, Australian property, crypto. That is the carry trade, and estimates of its size run anywhere from $500bn to well over $4tn depending on what you count. The trade has one fatal property: it makes money quietly for years and loses it all at once, because a rising yen simultaneously raises the cost of your debt and cuts the value of what you bought with it, forcing you to sell the good assets to repay the cheap loan. That is precisely what happened in August 2024, when a single BoJ move took the Nikkei down 12.4 per cent in a day and dragged everything else with it. So the question is not whether Japan raises rates - it is whether the exit is orderly. We have opened a forecast on the transmission rather than on the decision: an 8 per cent yen appreciation inside any thirty-day window before March, at 28 per cent.
brief.context: Date the rail: this one runs back to 1999, when the Bank of Japan took policy rates to zero, and to 2013, when quantitative and qualitative easing made the yen the world's designated funding currency by policy rather than by accident. The permit that changed is inflation - Japan spent a generation unable to generate it and now has it, imported partly through a weak currency and partly through an energy bill that this year's Hormuz disruption has made worse, which is the link back to the top of this brief. The desk that decides is the BoJ policy board, but the desk that transmits is the leveraged fund complex and the Japanese life insurers and pension funds who hold enormous foreign bond portfolios and hedge them in the currency market. Base rate, stated before the inside view: moves of 8 per cent or more in the yen inside thirty days have happened roughly five times in twenty years - 2008, 2016, late 2022, August 2024 - so about once every four years, which over a seven-month window prices near 15 per cent before adjusting for a live hiking cycle. The honest counter is that Japan has repeatedly signalled tightening and then delivered less than markets priced, and each disappointment has weakened rather than snapped the carry. The falsifier is dated: a hold on 18 September with the yen back above 160 by mid-October would say the market front-ran a move that is not coming.

angles.effect: Gain, and they are the constituency this is actually for. A stronger yen cuts an imported food and energy bill that has been the single most unpopular fact of Japanese economic life for three years.

angles.party: Japanese exporters and the equity index
angles.effect: Pay. A generation of earnings guidance is built on a weak currency, which is why every previous tightening attempt has met organised resistance from the part of the economy that appears in the index.
Pay the fastest and with the least warning. The characteristic damage is not in Japan at all - it lands in emerging-market bonds, crypto and momentum equities, the assets bought with borrowed yen.

Faces a genuine two-sided effect worth stating rather than resolving: Japanese investors are among the largest foreign holders of Treasuries, and higher yields at home give them a reason to bring money back at exactly the moment American issuance is heaviest.

dec.kill: A hold on 18 September, or a hike accompanied by explicit guidance that it is the last one, with the yen drifting back above 160 - that would establish this as another false start in a long series. Conversely, a hike delivered alongside a break through 150 would confirm the transmission leg and is the tripwire we have armed against it.

consp.claim: That the carry unwind is the mechanism by which the everything bubble finally breaks, and that authorities know it - the circulating version holds that the August 2024 episode was a rehearsal, that the true size of the borrowed-yen stack is deliberately not published, and that a coordinated intervention is being prepared to be presented as a rescue after the damage rather than before it.
consp.spread: A long-running staple of the /biz/ market threads and of doomer-finance blogging, with headlines in that genre this month running to phrases like markets brace for carry trade chaos and the day the yen stopped being money; it overlaps heavily with the same audience that circulates the long-end and yield-control claims.
consp.read: The hidden-fragility frame, and its kernel is unusually respectable: nobody actually knows the size of the carry stack, the published estimates genuinely span an order of magnitude, and the August 2024 episode really did transmit a Tokyo rate decision into a global drawdown within hours. The unsupported step is the coordination claim. Central banks being late is the overwhelmingly documented pattern - the firemen usually arrive after the fire, not because they planned it - and our own standing hypothesis on rescues is written the other way round: when consensus is certain a rescue is coming, raise the odds it is late or absent. That is a testable expectation rather than a plot.

brief.head: Putin says a Ukraine deal is possible as Britain summons his envoy
brief.h: Speaking at the Eastern Economic Forum in Russia's Far East, President Putin said there was a chance of reaching an agreement to end the war, that a number of countries including the United States and China were ready to support a settlement, and - the detail that carries the most information - that contacts with Kyiv do exist and are continuing on an ongoing basis, primarily through intelligence channels, before adding that ultimately the problem must be resolved by the countries involved; Ukraine's foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said he expected a new dynamic in peace efforts and India's S. Jaishankar offered help days after Narendra Modi told Putin the war needed to end, while on the same day Britain summoned Russia's charge d'affaires over the drone attack on Leipzig airport that Germany formally attributed to Moscow last week.
brief.t: Strip the speech and keep the one sentence that is expensive to say. Leaders offer peace rhetorically for free all the time; what Putin did today was confirm a working back-channel - contacts continuing on an ongoing basis, primarily through intelligence channels - six days after his own spokesman described negotiations as being in a deep pause with no new proposals whatsoever. Those two statements cannot both be complete, and the second one is the cheap one to make. Wars end when both sides' estimates of the future converge, and the machinery through which that convergence gets tested is almost never a foreign ministry - it is exactly this kind of intelligence-service channel, which is how Korea in 1953 and most modern armistices were actually built. But notice what Putin refused in his next breath: he handed the problem back to the two belligerents, which is a polite way of declining every third-party mechanism on offer, including the guarantee architecture that is the only thing Kyiv would sign for. Our ceasefire forecast moves from 13 to 15 percent - a small move, because the same day produced its own counterweight in London summoning Russia's envoy over a bombed airport in Germany.
brief.context: The rail here is a war-termination pattern rather than a diplomatic one. Roughly two-thirds of interstate wars end by negotiated settlement, and the strongest single predictor of a successful negotiation is a stalemate that both sides perceive - the operative word being perceive, since Moscow spent last week publicly claiming gains at Pokrovsk and Kupiansk, which tells you where its expectations still sit. The base rate cuts against speed: about 79 per cent of interstate wars end within two years, and this one is at four and a half, which puts it in the tail where wars stop for reasons of exhaustion and internal politics rather than of bargaining. Two clocks are running underneath. Moscow's is domestic and industrial - this week the Russian government took control of another private manufacturer, which is what a war economy looks like when it runs out of slack. Europe's is the punishment track: Germany closes the Russian consulate-general in Bonn on 18 September over Leipzig, Britain has now summoned Moscow's envoy over the same incident, and Russia has promised to mirror both. Expulsions are cheap, which is precisely why states reach for them, and a coalition busy expelling diplomats is not a coalition about to underwrite a guarantee. The falsifier we would accept is concrete rather than atmospheric: Russia accepting any limited ceasefire - it rejected even a Black Sea one - would be a genuine reversal and would move this number hard.

angles.effect: Gains the appearance of reasonableness at zero cost, addressed less to Kyiv than to Washington, Delhi and Beijing - the audience whose continued purchases and diplomatic cover fund the war. Naming the US and China as supporters of a settlement is flattery aimed at the two governments that could raise his costs.

Gains a talking point and carries a risk. Welcoming a new dynamic keeps Ukraine inside a process it cannot afford to be seen leaving, while the same intelligence-channel format is the one Ukrainian commentary fears most, because a channel that excludes foreign ministries can also exclude Ukraine.
Gains standing cheaply. Offering to help end a war you are not fighting, while continuing to buy the oil that funds it, is a low-cost bid for the mediator role that pays regardless of the outcome.

Pay for the attribution they made. Having named Russia over Leipzig, they now have to sustain a punishment track through a winter in which their own energy costs are the highest in three years - and cheap measures are the ones that get chosen.
Pay in the interval. Every week the process is described as promising is another week of strikes on the grid before the heating season, and the tempo has not changed since the talks did.

dec.kill: Russia accepting any limited ceasefire - maritime, energy-infrastructure or aerial - which it has consistently refused, including the Black Sea proposal. That single reversal would be worth more than any number of forum statements. Conversely, a Kremlin repetition of the deep pause formulation within a fortnight would establish today as ordinary positioning and retrace the move.

consp.claim: That a deal is being finalised over Ukraine's head - that the intelligence-channel contacts Putin described are the real negotiation, that a draft is already largely agreed from earlier rounds, and that Kyiv will be presented with terms rather than consulted on them.
consp.spread: Unusually, this circulates as much in mainstream Ukrainian commentary and among European officials as on the boards; reporting has described concerns in Kyiv about backchannel discussions between Moscow and Washington that exclude Ukraine and its allies, and the same claim runs in a harder form on X and Telegram.
consp.read: The great-powers-decide frame, which is the oldest reading in European diplomacy and here has a large checkable core: the channel exists because Putin just confirmed it, envoy-level meetings with Moscow have taken place outside the formal track, and the format itself - spy services rather than diplomats - is designed to exclude. What it cannot establish is the content, and the counter-evidence is real: Ukraine has repeatedly been the party that blocked terms it disliked, which is not the behaviour of a state being handed a fait accompli. The honest version is that the fear is structurally reasonable and the specific claim is unproven, and the observable that would settle it is whether any announced framework arrives with Kyiv's signature on it or without.

brief.head: Sanchez denies Morocco steered Ceuta as police tell a judge it did
brief.h: Addressing parliament on 3 September, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said his government had received no alerts or special notices before 30-31 July, when an estimated sixty to seventy thousand people crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, and said there was no solid proof whatsoever that Morocco had planned the breach; a Spanish National Police report submitted to a judge alleges that Moroccan security personnel helped direct the crossing as a coordinated operation, and police intelligence is reported to have issued warnings on 28 and 29 July, the second reportedly sent to the Secretariat of State for Security warning of extreme risk of a mass crossing by sea or fence in the final days of the month; Spain says 69,500 people were returned to Morocco and describes the returns as voluntary, while Vox is pushing to activate Article 102 of the constitution to put the prime minister on trial and conservative and far-right MEPs rallied against Madrid in Strasbourg this week.
brief.t: There are two separate claims in this story and the government is being attacked on the wrong one. Whether Rabat organised the crossing is genuinely unresolved - a police report submitted to a judge is an allegation under examination, not a finding. Whether Madrid was warned is a documentary question with a paper trail, and that is the one that will decide Sanchez's position, because a government can survive being coerced by a neighbour and cannot easily survive having been told and done nothing. The system underneath is the one worth learning, because it is spreading. Migration has become a low-cost coercive instrument: a state that hosts people another state does not want can generate a crisis by doing nothing - by simply standing its border guards down for an afternoon - and there is no treaty violation to point at, no attributable act, and no proportionate military response available. Follow what it buys. In 2021 Morocco opened the same border after Spain hosted a Polisario leader, and within a year Madrid had reversed sixty years of policy and endorsed Moroccan autonomy over Western Sahara. If that is the template, the price this time is not the returns - it is whatever Rabat asks for next, and the honest alternative explanation is that a Spanish Supreme Court ruling on 8 July, which stopped summary returns of people arriving by sea, plus viral posts, produced a crowd nobody had to organise at all.
brief.context: The rail predates the headline by exactly five years, which is what makes a deliberate read admissible here rather than speculative: the May 2021 Ceuta episode is a documented precedent with a documented payoff, and the mechanism has a name in the literature - Kelly Greenhill's coercive engineered migration, in which population movements are generated or threatened to extract concessions from states with liberal asylum obligations. Spain is unusually exposed to it because Ceuta and Melilla are EU territory on the African mainland with a land border a few kilometres long, and because Morocco holds three levers at once: migration, fisheries and counter-terrorism cooperation. The desk that decides is not the foreign ministry on either side - it is the Moroccan interior ministry and the royal palace, and on the Spanish side the Secretariat of State for Security, which is precisely the office the leaked warnings were reportedly addressed to. The base rate deserves stating with its caveat: Greenhill's dataset finds that most attempts of this kind extract at least partial concessions, which is a striking finding and also a single-author dataset with real selection problems, since attempts that failed quietly are the hardest cases to observe. Two observables would settle the story - publication of the two dated police intelligence notes, and whether any Spanish concession to Morocco appears in the next twelve months on Western Sahara, fisheries or customs.

angles.effect: Gains from keeping the question on Moroccan intent, where the evidence is contested, rather than on internal warnings, where it is documentary. Saying there is no solid proof whatsoever about Rabat is a narrower statement than it sounds and does not address what the interior ministry knew.

Gains either way, which is the elegance of the instrument. If it organised the crossing it has demonstrated leverage at no attributable cost; if it merely failed to police the coast it has demonstrated the same leverage with even less exposure - and it has said nothing that can be quoted.

Gain the year's most useful issue and are overreaching it. The evidenced charge - that warnings existed and were not acted on - is politically lethal on its own; the constitutional-trial and treason framing is far weaker and lets the government answer the wrong accusation.

Pay and have no seat. Sixty-nine thousand five hundred returns described as voluntary is a legal characterisation doing heavy work, and it is the category the July court ruling was about in the first place.
Carries the precedent. If a neighbouring state can generate an EU border crisis on demand and be paid to stop, every state on the Union's periphery has learned the price list.

dec.kill: Publication of the two police intelligence notes dated 28 and 29 July with their distribution lists - that settles the warnings question in one document, in either direction. On the coercion question, the observable is a Spanish concession to Morocco within twelve months on Western Sahara, fisheries or customs; its absence would be real evidence that this was a court ruling plus a crowd rather than an operation.

consp.claim: That the prime minister engineered the crisis himself - Vox and its spokespeople have alleged that Sanchez is prolonging it to justify suspending the next general election, that he is acting as a Moroccan agent, and that the endgame is ceding Ceuta to Morocco; none of these accusations has been accompanied by evidence. Separately, an ethnic-scapegoat narrative is circulating around the Ceuta crossings, and media analysts have linked part of its amplification to bot networks.
consp.spread: The first set is not fringe at all - it comes from the leadership of Spain's third-largest party and was carried into the European Parliament this week; the second circulates on X, Telegram and Spanish-language boards, at volumes large enough that fact-checkers and researchers have written about the amplification pattern rather than the content.
consp.read: Two techniques worth naming separately. The first is unfalsifiable escalation: the charge is not that the government failed, which is checkable, but that it intends something it has not done yet, which cannot be disproved until the election is either called or not - and note that the checkable version of the criticism is much stronger, which is the tell that the escalation is doing political rather than evidentiary work. The second is the scapegoat template, and the useful thing for a reader is the mechanics rather than the content: a real grievance about a border failure is attached to a group identity, the attachment is amplified faster than any correction can travel, and the amplification is measurably inorganic. We report the existence and the technique and do not repeat the claim, because the belief is the data here and the content is not.

lesson: Today's lesson is a mechanism with a name, and once you have it you will see it in half a dozen borders. The political scientist Kelly Greenhill called it coercive engineered migration - the use, or the threatened use, of population movements as an instrument of statecraft. It works on a specific kind of target: a state with liberal asylum obligations, a free press and a domestic opposition, because those three things convert a crowd at a fence into a governing crisis within about forty-eight hours. And its elegance is that the coercer need not act at all. A neighbouring state can generate the entire effect by omission - by standing its border patrols down for one afternoon - which leaves no treaty violated, nothing attributable, and no proportionate response available, since you cannot bomb a country for failing to police a beach. Greenhill assembled roughly fifty-six cases since 1951 and found that most attempts extracted at least partial concessions, which is a striking number and one worth handling carefully: it is a single-author dataset, and quiet failures are exactly the cases hardest to observe, so treat it as a strong indication rather than a settled rate. The clearest worked example is the one directly behind today's Ceuta story. In May 2021 Morocco let several thousand people swim around the same breakwater after Spain hosted a Polisario leader for medical treatment; within a year Madrid had reversed six decades of policy and endorsed Moroccan autonomy over Western Sahara. That is what the instrument buys. So here is what it predicts now, in a form you can score: if the July crossing was coercion rather than an accident of a court ruling and a viral post, the payment will not be visible at the border - it will appear over the next twelve months as a Spanish concession on Western Sahara, on fisheries access, or on customs at Ceuta and Melilla. If a year passes with no such concession, the coercion read was wrong and the boring explanation was right. That is the honest test, and it is the reason to learn the mechanism rather than to pick a side in the row about it.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz
events.note: Fourth consecutive night of US strikes on air defences, radars, maritime assets and mine-laying capability around the strait. Transits fell to as few as six vessels in a day against a ten-day average near thirteen and a pre-war norm around eighty-five

events.label: Kuhestak, Hormozgan
events.note: A US strike hit a house holding a wedding here on 1-2 September along with a nearby telecommunications tower, killing four named civilians including a four-year-old and wounding more than sixty. CENTCOM contested the sourcing of the report, not the strike

events.label: Ahmed al-Jaber AB, Kuwait
events.note: Iran's army claims missiles and suicide drones against satellite communications, equipment warehouses and fighter hangars here. Kuwait's army confirmed it was engaging the attack; no host-state confirmation of damage, which is the honest limit of what is known

events.label: Al Minhad AB, UAE
events.note: Iran claims strikes on US positions and radar systems here - the Emirates becoming the sixth host state to take fire in this war, and the newest surface on which an interception-dependent equilibrium can fail

events.label: Kharg Island
events.note: Still undamaged and still the subject of the 30 September falsifier clock. Handles about 90 per cent of Iranian crude exports; the March raid hit military sites here and deliberately spared the loading terminals

events.label: Ceuta
events.note: Sanchez told parliament there were no advance alerts before the 30-31 July crossing of some sixty to seventy thousand people, while a National Police report to a judge alleges Moroccan security personnel helped direct it and two dated police warnings are reported to have gone to the interior ministry

events.label: Leipzig/Halle Airport
events.note: Britain summoned Russia's charge d'affaires today over the 4 August explosive drone at the airport used to move munitions to Ukraine, widening the attribution Germany made last week. Berlin closes the Bonn consulate on 18 September; Moscow promises to mirror

events.label: Rotterdam / TTF hub
events.note: Dutch front-month gas near a three-year high with EU storage around 62 per cent, some 17 points below the seasonal norm and the thinnest for the date since records began in 2011. Roughly a fifth of world LNG normally transits Hormuz

events.label: Vladivostok
events.note: Putin told the Eastern Economic Forum there is a chance of an agreement and confirmed contacts with Kyiv continue on an ongoing basis, primarily through intelligence channels - six days after his spokesman called negotiations a deep pause with no proposals whatsoever

events.label: Odesa
events.note: Russia continues striking port export facilities and the energy grid before the heating season while the diplomatic track is described as promising. Tempo has not changed since the language did

events.label: Tokyo
events.note: Yen to a one-month high of 156.15 on rate-rise bets before the 18 September BoJ decision; ten-year JGB near 3 per cent, the highest since 1996. The world's cheap funding leg is repricing and the transmission runs through every asset bought with borrowed yen

events.label: Beijing
events.note: Twenty-one days to the Xi state visit, with Washington preparing a 7.5 per cent overcapacity tariff layer sized to land exactly on the 20 per cent ceiling Beijing says it was promised. China pulled out of the Gwangju Biennale over a Taiwan exhibition - symbolic friction, not a quarantine signal

fired: NO NEW FIRE today, and the 1 September Hormuz fire is NOT re-counted. That wire fired on the stricter 27 August wording - an attack on a US-flagged or US-escorted vessel, or an attack Iran publicly claims - and dating a fire exactly once is the whole point of having narrowed it. A fourth night of exchanges is continuation of a fired wire, not a new one

NOT fired, and it remains the limit of everything above: no struck US-flagged hull, no confirmed American death. Iran put its fire into Kuwaiti and Emirati air bases and Kuwait's army confirmed it was engaging missiles and drones launched from Iran. The intercepted-volley equilibrium has now held for a fourth night, and it is arithmetic rather than restraint

NOT fired, checked and logged so each non-fire is scoreable: no blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank; no strike on Kharg's loading terminals; no awarded dredging or terminal contract in Venezuela; no concrete poured past the prohibited level at Kishanganga; no Kremlin acceptance of any limited ceasefire; no Taiwan mobilization indicator; no EU emergency intervention in the gas market

WIRE HYGIENE - the board has now taken fire on six host states and had no wire covering the hosts' own politics, which is the surface where this escalation actually converts into a political event. Corrected below. A second gap, on the yen funding leg, is corrected at the same time and paid for with a new forecast rather than only with a wire

Data gap: GDELT was unreachable (URLError) on both tested keywords - Strait of Hormuz and gold reserves - for the THIRD consecutive session. Recorded as a gap, not as zero. Three dark sessions running makes this a failed instrument rather than an outage, and the honest consequence is that the news-volume channel has contributed nothing to any update this week
armed: NEW - Gulf host defection: a GCC government publicly restricting US offensive use of its territory or airspace, or formally conditioning basing on de-escalation talks with Tehran, before 15 December. That is the observable that converts a venue into a party, and it is the sequel nobody is pricing

NEW - BoJ 18 September: a policy-rate rise accompanied by USD/JPY through 150. That is the confirmation leg on the newly opened GEO-025, and the point at which a Tokyo rate decision becomes a global margin call
A struck US-flagged hull or a confirmed American death - the falsifier on the whole intercepted-volley equilibrium, and still the only escalation trigger left unfired in the strait

An Iranian strike that kills nationals of a Gulf host state rather than only targeting US facilities on their soil. That is what would convert Kuwait, the Emirates, Bahrain and Jordan from venues into parties

A war-risk re-rating of the southern Hormuz corridor by the Joint War Committee, or a withdrawal of the US clearance claim - the actuarial event that governs GEO-001 far more than any diplomatic announcement
A strike on Kharg's LOADING terminals as opposed to its military sites - it would convert the 30 August video from theatre into a warning order and re-rate GEO-001, GEO-003 and GEO-009 together
Europe/energy: an EU emergency intervention in the gas market before 15 November - a price cap, mandatory demand curtailment, or a storage-target waiver

Publication of the US overcapacity finding with the 7.5 per cent layer actually imposed before 24 September - versus a quiet delay past the summit. That single observable separates a coalition standard being built from a chip being waved

An awarded, funded dredging contract or dedicated heavy-crude terminal tender in the Orinoco or Lake Maracaibo channel - what GEO-022 resolves on, and the line between opportunistic spoils and a pre-built heavy-barrel rail
Publication of the two Spanish police intelligence notes dated 28 and 29 July with their distribution lists - the document that settles the Ceuta warnings question in either direction
A failed or heavily tailed JGB or gilt auction - the point at which the long-end repricing stops being a price move and becomes a funding event
Scholar-owned: IRGC/Basij defection (Takeyh) - casualty-recruitment crossover (Kofman) - PLA purge tempo (Fravel)

watch: Whether any Gulf host government confirms physical damage at Ahmed al-Jaber or Al Minhad. Iran claims hangars, warehouses and radars; Kuwait has confirmed only that it was engaging the attack. The launch is confirmed and the effect is not, and that gap is the whole evidentiary question tonight

Whether Brent posts a daily CLOSE above $100 before 24 September. It touched the high nineties intraday today and our band forecast fell from 51 to 32 per cent on that geometry alone - this is the first question on the board that can resolve, and it is our first Brier score

Whether the Bank of Japan raises on 18 September and where the yen sits a week later. A hike with the yen through 150 is the transmission leg on the new carry forecast; a hold with the yen back above 160 says the market front-ran a move that is not coming

Whether the two Spanish police intelligence notes dated 28 and 29 July are published with their distribution lists. Whether Rabat organised the Ceuta crossing is contested; whether Madrid was warned is documentary, and only one of those two questions has a paper trail

Whether the Kremlin repeats the deep pause formulation within a fortnight. Putin confirmed today that intelligence-channel contacts are continuing; if Peskov walks that back on schedule, today was positioning and the two-point raise retraces
